findings.title: Fixed reviewer identity resolution does not authenticate who authored the PASS payload
findings.evidence: The registry check correctly resolves the identity string to a fixed, hash-pinned record containing a real Codex thread ID, and the unregistered-identity negative test reaches that check and rejects. However, the passing test constructs the peerReview PASS object itself and sets reviewer.identity to the known registered string. The projector checks equality to the record but has no signed review assertion, authenticated author channel, or app-resolved review event proving that this thread authored the submitted peerReview JSON. A different caller can copy the same registered identity string and construct the same PASS payload.
findings.impact: The fix establishes registered identity-string matching, not proof of peer authorship or genuine review execution. Do not interpret this validator or test harness as authenticated independent acceptance.
findings.repair: Bind the peer result to an authenticated review workflow record, signed attestation, or other trusted event proving the registered principal authored the exact candidate-bound review. If only identity registration is intended, rename the result/claims so they do not assert an actual independent PASS.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: A caller that copies the registered thread ID and submits a forged PASS is rejected; a genuine workflow-authenticated review record bound to the exact candidate and postimages is accepted.

findings.title: The workflow root is caller-selected, so owner-choice checks can run against a synthetic repository snapshot
findings.evidence: projectMediaPdp0SemanticCaseBatches accepts repositoryRoot from its caller and hashes workflow files found under that root without resolving it to the actual canonical checkout or a trusted source service. The positive harness creates a temporary root, copies the authority map and fixed peer registry, writes a synthetic PXD-998 decision section and owner-choice JSON, writes a peerReview PASS JSON, and the test expects projection to succeed. The harness labels this test-only and claims no signature, but the same root selection and structural checks are available to a production caller.
findings.impact: A structurally valid caller-created PXD and owner-choice record can be mistaken for an actual source owner workflow record if this projector's returned review fields are treated as authority evidence.
findings.repair: Bind workflow resolution to an externally trusted repository root/source snapshot and owner decision record; do not treat hashes computed from a caller-selected temporary root as owner authorization. Keep test fixture success explicitly separated from authority acceptance.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: A synthetic temporary repository with copied authority data and a caller-authored PXD choice cannot produce an authority-bearing projection; the exact canonical owner workflow record is resolved from a trusted root and its authorship/authority is independently established.

findings.title: The Draft 2020-12 schema accepts reversed numeric bounds
findings.evidence: Ajv strict validation accepts a bounded-number parameter with minimum=2 and maximum=1. The registry candidate states minimum must be less than or equal to maximum, but that relation is not enforced by the current Draft 2020-12 schema or a companion semantic validator.
findings.impact: The schema is structurally valid but does not by itself validate a nonempty numeric interval. Such a profile would reject every value and remain unusable, even though it passes registry-entry validation.
findings.repair: Add a repository-native semantic check for minimum <= maximum (and any selected step consistency) after schema validation; keep all bound values owner-supplied.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: The validator rejects reversed bounds and accepts a finite owner-specified interval with a resolvable owner unit and meaning reference.
